::: {#exr-piecewise}
## A piecewise function

::: {.lm-solution}
1. Both pieces are continuous; at $x = 1$, the left piece gives $1$, the right one tends to $a - 1$. So $f$ is continuous for $a = 2$.

1. Yes: the derivative of the left piece at $1$ is $2 \cdot 1 = 2$, that of the right piece is $a = 2$.
:::
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
All functions of this sheet are written for clarity, not for speed.
:::

::: {#exr-bisection}
## Bisection

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
bisection <- function(f, a, b, n) {
  midpoints <- numeric(n)
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    m <- (a + b) / 2
    midpoints[k] <- m
    if (sign(f(m)) == sign(f(a))) {
      a <- m
    } else {
      b <- m
    }
  }
  midpoints
}
```
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
midpoints <- bisection(function(x) cos(x) - x, 0, 1, 50)
errors <- abs(midpoints[1:40] - midpoints[50])
plot(1:40, errors, log = "y", type = "b", xlab = "step", ylab = "error")
```

After $n$ steps, the interval has the length $2^{-n}$, so the error falls along a straight line. Ten correct digits need $2^{-n} < 10^{-10}$, that is $n \geq 34$.
:::
:::
